### Arguments UMAP

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--min_dist`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The effective minimum distance between embedded points. Smaller values will result
in a more clustered/clumped embedding where nearby points on the manifold are drawn
closer together, while larger values will result on a more even dispersal of points.
The value should be set relative to the spread value, which determines the scale at
which embedded points will be spread out.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.5`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0.0`

[Max]{.arg-key} `10.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--spread`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The effective scale of embedded points. In combination with `min_dist` this
determines how clustered/clumped the embedded points are.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0.0`

[Max]{.arg-key} `10.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--num_components`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of dimensions of the embedding.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `2`

[Min]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_iter`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of iterations (epochs) of the optimization. Called `n_epochs`
in the original UMAP. Default is set to 500 if
neighbors['connectivities'].shape[0] <= 10000, else 200.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0`

[Max]{.arg-key} `1000`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alpha`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The initial learning rate for the embedding optimization.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--gamma`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Weighting applied to negative samples in low dimensional embedding optimization.
Values higher than one will result in greater weight being given to negative samples.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--negative_sample_rate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of negative samples to select per positive sample
in the optimization process. Increasing this value will result
in greater repulsive force being applied, greater optimization
cost, but slightly more accuracy.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `5`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--init_pos`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
How to initialize the low dimensional embedding. Called `init` in the original UMAP. Options are:

* Any key from `.obsm`
* `'paga'`: positions from `paga()`
* `'spectral'`: use a spectral embedding of the graph
* `'random'`: assign initial embedding positions at random.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"spectral"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"paga"`, `"spectral"`, `"random"`
:::
::::
:::::

### Arguments densMAP

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--lambda`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Controls the regularization weight of the density correlation term in densMAP.
Higher values prioritize density preservation over the UMAP objective, and vice versa
for values closer to zero. Setting this parameter to zero is equivalent to running
the original UMAP algorithm.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `2.0`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0.01`

[Max]{.arg-key} `10.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--fraction`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Controls the fraction of epochs (between 0 and 1) where the density-augmented objective
is used in densMAP. The first (1 - dens_frac) fraction of epochs optimize the original
UMAP objective before introducing the density correlation term.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.3`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_shift`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
A small constant added to the variance of local radii in the embedding when calculating
the density correlation objective to prevent numerical instability from dividing by a
small number.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.1`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/dimred/densmap/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/dimred/densmap);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/dimred/densmap/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
